Vault write contract: preflight (read-only fingerprint, schema, pinned ruleset and SysML v2.0 library manifest; no write on mismatch); build a typed semantic graph; stage a complete manifest of additions, changes and deletions in a disposable directory; validate and preview the diff before atomic publish; failed validation leaves the approved vault untouched; canonical semantic files stay separate from view/layout metadata and reports; record a run manifest (fixture hash, timestamps, tool/rule/library versions, disposition totals, validation results, exceptions, file hashes, changeset, rollback reference).

Merge by field ownership: EA owns source semantics, BOM owns versioned BOM evidence, MDSE owns canonical IDs, placement and derived projections, users own local annotations. Never silently overwrite manually edited semantic content. Reimport reconciles by (source system, source GUID, semantic role) to a stable target ID with a three-way comparison against the last-generated baseline, detecting source-changed, user-changed and concurrent change separately. Removal or relocation only through a tombstone/redirect plan.

Rule: Failure levels: Fatal stop (unreadable/corrupt QEAX, source/profile/hash mismatch, unusable identities, evidence or provenance loss, ledger/count corruption, no coherent navigable vault, unexpected diagram access, unsafe overwrite, unparseable core model, untraceable drops). Localized semantic problems flag and continue. Warnings (missing optional multiplicity or metadata, formatting) log and continue. One parser rejection never poisons a batch: isolate it, write an MDSE fallback, revalidate, proceed.

Zero-silent-loss: every source record reconciles exactly once into native, alias_merged, evidence_only, deferred_review, excluded_by_policy or error. Unrecoverable omission, unauthorized deletion, silent deduplication, failed note-link resolution and conflicting-edit overwrite are export blockers. BOM reader preserves rejected rows (position and value), never rounds decimals, infers units, or omits formulas, revisions or effectivity.

Review changes are recorded as a git diff against the baseline import commit, with reasons in Review Changes Log.md. An AI turns them into rule changes.
Import is mechanical. The importer applies the Ruleset and does not interpret.
Every change to an existing file is listed in one dated changelog per import run. Each entry links the changed file, describes the change, and flags any conflict.
Importing the same input again produces no changes and no changelog entries.
A run is complete only when every planned entity reaches an explicit terminal state: written, intentionally suppressed by rule, or explicitly failed. There is no unexplained remainder.
Import is additive. An import never deletes existing content.
An empty YAML property may be filled by an import.
Content that does not match existing body content is added to the body.
A change to any existing value requires approval, including EA-owned fields. Approval is given before the run (pre-approval, by field selection in the Start step) or after the run (review approval).
Pre-approval applies to all notes in the run.

A conflict is content that contradicts existing YAML, v2, or body content and is not approved for change. It is not applied. It is listed in the body with a `flagConflict` callout for engineer review.
An engineer resolves a conflict by approving a change or by selecting the correct data by hand.
A source record that disappears is reported with a `flagImport` callout. It is not deleted. This applies to EA-owned relationships.

Element family mapping (60 exact EA type/stereotype families = 40 native definition + 7 local usage/behavior + 13 non-native): Requirement variants to RequirementDefinition; Activity variants to ActionDefinition; UseCase to UseCaseDefinition; State to StateDefinition; Class variants (Hardware/Physical/Software Component, block, Module, Platform, Business Line, unstereotyped) to PartDefinition; System Partner and Actor to external PartDefinition; Object to PartDefinition (valid prior classifier becomes specialization, not typing); interface Classes to InterfaceDefinition; Generic Physical Interface to PortDefinition; Logical/Physical Signal to ItemDefinition; Software Parameter to AttributeDefinition; testCase to VerificationCaseDefinition; Constraint to ConstraintDefinition; Event to OccurrenceDefinition; Physical Context to PartDefinition (composite) or external PartDefinition (single).

Local usages: Action, Part and Port become owned usages (untyped allowed with UNRESOLVED_ACTION_TYPE, UNRESOLVED_PART_TYPE, UNRESOLVED_PORT_TYPE); Part:FlowProperty becomes an ItemUsage owned by the port; StateNode becomes a StateUsage; Synchronization becomes fork/join from actual control-flow evidence; Trigger becomes a transition trigger.

Non-native: Package = folder only; InformationItem, Note, Issue, Change, Decision, Text = MDSE notes with YAML links (no inferred executable branching); Artifact:Image and Artifact:Document = attachments referenced in element YAML; Sequence = reference-only workflow view; ProxyConnector = reference to the original connection; Boundary = aggregate evidence note (STEP-00 2 revises the earlier removal).

Connector family mapping (26 families, 14,688 connectors): Generalization to specialization; Abstraction:allocate to allocation; Aggregation to owned PartUsage where physical containment is evidenced, else review; Dependency:satisfy to satisfy; Realisation to perform/allocate by endpoint kinds, else review; refine to Dependency + Refinement metadata; Association to ConnectionUsage only if connectivity is proven; UseCase:extend to optional case usage; UseCase:include to required nested case usage; ControlFlow to Succession with guards; StateFlow to transition; Nesting to approved nested usage else organizational; NoteLink to YAML links only; Sequence reference-only; Usage to generic Dependency; Dependency:verify to verification; Connector to port-to-port ConnectionUsage; Realisation:deriveReqt takes precedence over generic Realisation. Eligibility is per connector, never per family.

Exact-family exceptions override wildcard selectors: shared/composite aggregation = owned typed usage (a non-owning ref part only for an existing occurrence); untyped Part/Action/Port allowed with review flags; InformationItem = MDSE note, not ItemDefinition; Physical Context needs composition evidence; Object classifier = specialization, not typing; Copy alias only with proven identity; Binding only for compatible equal features, else flagLink; include = required nested usage, extend = optional conditional usage; Event = OccurrenceDefinition; quantities and units need explicit source evidence (never infer unit from name); requirement nesting is not derivation or folder hierarchy; unresolved connectors get a persistent per-source flagLink. The approved-version resolver refuses wildcard fallback.

Tagged values follow `governance/schemas/ea-tag-dispositions.json` (the V1 list, 121 tags, decisions W-29 to W-106). Only `body` tags are written to `## Source: EA`. A value that is empty, `unassigned` or `<memo>` is never written, whatever its tag. A tag not in the list is kept in the body and reported as an import warning until it is given a disposition.

`## Source: EA` carries one EA GUID, the note's own, as the re-import identity. Usage, relationship, flow, trigger and connector lines carry no GUID; they name the other note. A flag callout keeps the connector GUID because it is the handle to the ledger row.

Rule: Structure, links, quantities and multiplicity are defined by the SysML v2 block and are not repeated in `## Source: EA`. Relationships SysML v2 has no form for, and identifying properties, stay in the YAML (`describes`, `eaType`, `uid`, `id`). `## Source: EA` holds only what is stored nowhere else: the note's EA GUID, the original name when the file name differs, alias, the kept tags, trigger and guard text, unresolved connectors and attachments. EA author, created date, type, stereotype and package are not written: the uid carries date and author, `eaType` carries type and stereotype, the folder carries the package.

A requirement's wording is the `doc /* … */` of its `requirement def` (EA Note plus `text` tags), and is not repeated in the note body. Anywhere the Workbench shows a requirement it shows name, subtype and text.

Transition trigger, guard and effect follow SysML v2: `transition first a accept t if g do e then b;` and `succession first a if g then b;`, with the wording in `doc` of helper usages. EA PDATA1/2/3 are trigger/guard/effect.

The importer page asks for the person's full name before anything can be built, derives the 13-character author code (MOD-002), remembers it in the browser, and uses it as the vault's `author`, as the author of every note created in the run, and for the person note in `99_System/04_People` of a new vault. The page shows a stage progress bar with a labelled list of stages (fingerprint, translate EA, map BOM, assemble, write), and ends with the Obsidian steps: open the vault, click "Trust author and enable plugins", let Bootstrap verify and enable, confirm with the Bootstrap command. An EA Port becomes a port usage written `port name : [~]PortDef[mult]`. The multiplicity is the Multiplicity field, read as for parts; `~` is written when the object has an `isConjugated` tag with a true value (EA storage of conjugation is unverified, so no other evidence is guessed). A port is typed by a port definition only: a Port whose Classifier is an interface definition is written without a type, the interface is kept as a `- Port <name> is typed by interface [[…]]` line in Source, and the usage is flagged (`UNRESOLVED_PORT_TYPE:TARGET_IS_INTERFACE_DEF`).

One reusable note per normalized internal part number; revisions and occurrences never duplicate it. Parent assembly owns BOM usages with counts, quantities and applicability. Where Used is a reverse query and is never materialized in the child. Separate discrete multiplicity from measured quantity and unit; preserve raw values; never guess units or double count.

One effective BOM per parent and configuration/revision. Competing simultaneous effective BOMs block automatic interpretation. Historical revisions stay in the source ledger. Family similarity is not automatically specialization, variation or substitutability.

A row with blank internal Part Number and populated Manufacturing Part Number is an alternate of the preceding primary line in the same parent, revision, configuration and BOM group. Consecutive rows attach to the same primary. It is not a child usage and adds no quantity. With no unambiguous preceding primary it is review-only. Acceptance: the three-line example yields 2 required PC-100 occurrences.
BOM-before-EA and EA-before-BOM imports must converge where supported (G5).

The vault holds the latest revision of each product in scope. Superseded revisions are not imported.
One note per PartNumber. A part's properties come from its latest revision.
A usage records the child revision pinned by the parent. Parent PN and line number identify a usage.
A PN whose latest revision cannot be determined is reported and not imported.
Revision strings are stored as exported, not normalized.
A child part's body lists each assembly that uses an older revision of it, with that usage.
A parent that pins a child revision different from the child's latest revision is flagged with `flagConflict`.
Alternate-part rows with a blank PN attach to the PN above them. They are not parts.
Drawing-only lines are recorded as document references and excluded from quantities.

The importer reads the BOM from `.xlsx`, `.csv` or `.tsv` in the page. Two layouts are recognised by header names: flat (Parent Part Number, Child Part Number, Linenumber, Amount, Unit …) and redline (Number, CL1, CL2, level columns 0..7 or Structure). Part numbers are read as text. In a redline, unstruck text in a cell is current and struck text is the previous value; a part number struck with no replacement is a removed line. A sheet with no recognised header is refused with the reason. The redline layout is inferred, not checked against a real file.

Each part number gets one `Object` (subtype part) note named `<PN>` (the part number alone, so the file name and the part number are the same value; the name is the H1 and a `- Name:` line in Source) under `BOM/Parts`: `part def P_<PN>` with `partNumber`, `revision` (CL1+CL2 as exported), `source`, `lifecycleState` attributes. The parent's block owns one part usage per line: whole-number counts with unit ea/piece become multiplicity; any other quantity is `quantity` plus the unit as written (case kept); line, pinned `childRevision`, reference designator, effectivity dates, SSC and notes are attributes. Drawing lines (name starts DWG) become a `Document` note under `BOM/Drawings` referenced from the parent and are not usages. Alternate-source rows attach to the line above. Parent note lists children in `hasPart`.

The latest revision of a part number is the one it has as an assembly, or the one every parent pins when it is only a child. When there are several, or two revisions each have lines, the part number and the lines that use it are not imported and an error finding names the revisions (BOM-009, BOM-002). A parent pinning an older child revision gets a `flagConflict`; the child's body lists its older-revision users. Part numbers already noted in the vault are left as they are. Findings go to `99_System/11_Import/BOM Findings <date>.md`. EA to BOM matching by part number appearing in one EA element name is a report only.

The Edit lens adds relationships, elements and requirement text. Relationship kinds offered depend on the selected note's SysML definition; targets come from a searchable, folder-grouped browser limited to eligible notes. Structure and links are written into the source note's `## SysML v2` block (D-0003); a new note gets type, subtype, id, uid, status and its block only.

Every Edit-lens change is previewed as a diff, applied only on a click, refused when the file differs from what the preview was built from, written atomically (all files or none), and undoable while the files are unchanged.

A new note's id is the class prefix plus the highest existing number plus one (MOD-007); its uid is local time plus the author code from `.vault.yaml` and moves forward one millisecond on a clash (MOD-004). Without an author code, adding an element is refused.

A relationship can be selected from the Workbench list, a relationship table row or a canvas line (the canvas edge id carries the relationship's location) and then changed, given properties, or removed. The kinds that can be changed are those the Edit lens can add; any other member can only be removed or edited in the note.

Relationship properties are written inside the relationship in SysML: a `doc` comment, `attribute name = value;` (or `attribute name { doc … }` when the value is not a plain number or simple text), usage modifiers `ordered` and `nonunique`, quantity and direction. The drop-down offers only the options that relationship has; a free attribute name is accepted only where the relationship allows it (not specializes or verifies). Renaming a usage is refused when its name is used elsewhere in the block.

Every option in the Edit lens has a "?" that shows a short bundled definition with its options and a link to the language note (`99_System/04_Language`); nothing is fetched. A form being filled is not discarded when the index refreshes.

The Edit lens has a Ports tab for a part, item, port or interface definition. It adds, changes and removes: port definition features (`in|out|inout item|attribute|port`), port usages (`[ref] port p : [~]PortDef [mult] [ordered] [nonunique]`), interface definition ends (`end e : [~]PortDef`), connections (`connect`, `connection [n] [: Def] connect`, `interface [n] [: Def] connect`, with optional `end ::>` bindings), flows (`flow [n] [of Item] from a.x to b.y`) and bindings (`bind a.x = b.y`). Types are chosen in the searchable browser; paths are offered from the owner's parts and their ports. Every option has a "?".

The Ports tab checks before it previews: names are unique in the owner, a port or end is typed by a port definition, only items and attributes have a direction, a path must resolve through the owner's usages (inherited ones included), an interface connection joins ports, each port matches its end's type and conjugation, and a flow starts at an out (or inout) feature and ends at an in (or inout) one, with every `~` on the path reversing directions. Type or end mismatches that SysML allows (bound features of different types, both ports unconjugated) are shown as notes, not refusals. A member that has a body (properties, description) is not rewritten by the Ports tab.

The scanner reads every port form: `~`, `ref`, `:>` and `:>>` before or after the multiplicity, `ordered`, `nonunique`, directed features, interface and connection ends, and plain, `connection` and `interface` connects. Changing an owned usage in the Relationships tab keeps its `~`, `ref`, `:>` and `:>>`. After an apply or an undo the Edit lens redraws its lists from the new index without discarding a form being filled.
